post.description: The channel at `index` of `channels` gets a new key: the response carries its `keyId` and, only here, its `signingSecret`. Deliveries from now on (pending retries included) are signed with it; receivers tell the keys apart by `X-AIS-ITS-Key-Id`. A webhook from before 0.2.0 gets its first own key (it was signed with the deployment secret). 404 RULE_CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND for an index without channel, 422 RULE_CHANNEL_NOT_WEBHOOK for other channel types.

get.description: Visible alerts (the tenancy of GET /alerts) per local hour or day of `tz` of their first occurrence, counted by `groupBy`, every bucket from the one containing `from` to the one containing `to` (zeros included). Default range: 7 days (`1d`) or 24 hours (`1h`) up to now; at most 1000 buckets.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket size (at most 1000 buckets per request)

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: IANA time zone name of the bucket boundaries (local hours and days, e.g. WIB), any case; the response echoes the database spelling. UTC offsets such as `+07:00` are refused (use `Etc/GMT-7`), and so are names the database does not know (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`)

get.summary: Alert counts over time by severity, type or domain

get.description: The filters of GET /alerts, newest first, streamed (RFC 4180, UTF-8, CRLF). Column headers follow `Accept-Language` (`id`, default, or `en`); values are the stored codes, UTC ISO-8601 times and the English title and message. At most ALERT_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS rows (default 100 000): more matching alerts set `X-Truncated: true`.

X-Truncated.description: `true` when more alerts matched than the export carries

get.description: Every alert.raised.v1 stored in the alert: the one that opened it and each merged repeat or escalation, with its own time, severity, texts and measurements (`data`). Detectors publish no de-escalations (the kit's alert emitter only announces raises and escalations), so the history has none. Alerts stored before 0.2.0 have no history.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from `page.nextCursor` of the previous page

target.description: email: an address; telegram: a chat id or @channel; webhook: an http(s) URL receiving signed JSON POSTs

name.example: Pipeline danger to the operations room

scope.description: org: vessels of the organization; all: every vessel (only rules of an authority organization, written by its authority members). Default all for those, else org.

quietMinutes.description: Quiet period, minutes: an alert is not notified again by this rule within it unless its severity rises

orgId.description: Owning organization (super_admin only; default the active organization)

target.description: E-mail address, Telegram chat id / @channel, or webhook URL

keyId.description: Webhooks: id of the signing key, sent as `X-AIS-ITS-Key-Id`; null for other channels and for a webhook from before 0.2.0 (signed with the deployment secret, key id `deployment`, until its secret is rotated)

signingSecret.description: Webhooks: the HMAC-SHA256 signing secret, **only** in the response that created the key (POST, a PATCH adding the target, rotate-secret); store it at the receiver, it is never shown again. null otherwise

name.example: Pipeline danger to the operations room

scope.description: org: vessels of the organization; all: every vessel (authority rules)

total.description: Number of items across all pages

name.example: Pipeline danger to the operations room

scope.description: org: vessels of the organization; all: every vessel (only rules of an authority organization, written by its authority members). Default all for those, else org.

quietMinutes.description: Quiet period, minutes: an alert is not notified again by this rule within it unless its severity rises

target.description: E-mail address, Telegram chat id / @channel, or webhook URL

status.description: queued: the e-mail was handed to the e-mail pipeline (check the inbox)

keyId.description: Webhook tests: the X-AIS-ITS-Key-Id that signed the request — the key of the organization's channel with this target, `deployment` for a channel from before 0.2.0, or `test` (a throwaway key: the target is no channel yet, so the request proves reachability only); null for other channels

sent.description: Delivered (e-mail: accepted by the SMTP server)

pending.description: Waiting for their next attempt, or being attempted (`pending` and `sending`)

queued.description: E-mails handed to the e-mail pipeline, not yet sent

successRate.description: sent / (sent + failed), 4 decimals; null while none finished

severity.description: Alert severity when the delivery was planned

status.description: pending: waiting for an attempt; sending: attempt in progress; queued: e-mail handed to the e-mail pipeline; sent; failed: given up

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page

type.description: Alert type (registry ALERT_TYPES; future types possible)

severity.description: Highest severity of the merged occurrences

dedupKey.description: Occurrences with this key merge while unresolved

messageKey.description: Stable key of the text (`<domain>.<detector>.<situation>`, from `data.messageKey`) for clients that localize it; null when the detector sent none or an invalid one (render `title` / `message`)

messageParams.description: Values of the text (`data.messageParams`, flat strings, numbers and booleans); null together with `messageKey`

resolvedBy.description: User who resolved the alert; null while unresolved and when its detector resolved it (`resolutionEventId` set)

resolvedAt.description: When it was resolved: the action of the user, or the end of the condition (`resolvedAt` of `alert.resolved.v1`)

resolutionReason.example: safe: not at anchor within the warning distance
resolutionReason.description: Why the detector ended the condition (English `reason` of `alert.resolved.v1`); null otherwise

resolutionMessageKey.description: Localizable key of `resolutionReason` (`messageKey` in the data of `alert.resolved.v1`); null otherwise

resolutionMessageParams.description: Values of `resolutionMessageKey`; null together with it

resolutionEventId.description: Envelope id of the `alert.resolved.v1` that resolved the alert; null when a user resolved it or it is unresolved

byType.description: Every registry type (0 when none) plus any other type present

unread.description: Open alerts visible to the user stored or changed after `readUpTo` (all open alerts without a mark)

readUpTo.description: Read mark of the user in the active organization; null before the first POST /alerts/read

upTo.description: Alerts stored or changed up to this time (their `updatedAt`) count as read; default and maximum: now. The mark never moves backwards.

timeZone.description: Time zone of the bucket boundaries (database spelling)

keys.description: Keys of `counts`: every registry value of the dimension plus any other type present

eventId.description: Id of the alert.raised.v1 (the first one is the inbox alert id)

outcome.description: raised: opened the inbox alert; escalated: raised its severity; merged: a repeat

severity.description: Severity of this occurrence (the alert keeps the highest of its occurrences)

messageKey.description: Stable key of the text (`<domain>.<detector>.<situation>`, from `data.messageKey`) for clients that localize it; null when the detector sent none or an invalid one (render `title` / `message`)

messageParams.description: Values of the text (`data.messageParams`, flat strings, numbers and booleans); null together with `messageKey`

data.description: Measurements of the detector for this occurrence
